evidence_summary: Raw HTTP replay shows non-integer Request-Timeout headers ("3.5" and "abc") both accepted on POST /v2/vectordb/collections/list with http=200/code=0, identical to the integer control, violating the explicit contract that Request-Timeout must match ^[0-9]+$ with non-integer rejected (milvus_type_request_timeout_001, doc-archaeology from issue #49890 documenting exactly this float-silently-truncated / string-silently-ignored behavior).
rationale: Replay-capture semantic matching applies: two independent invalid-value reproductions plus a passing integer control give 1 successful reproduction + clear contract violation with a clear success signal (200/code=0 where rejection is asserted), i.e. a deterministic Type1 illegal-op-accepted (param_validation) rather than an intermittent or single-ambiguous-shot case, so the high-evidence path yields is_defect grade A score 9; the cross-endpoint borrowing of the header contract is acceptable because Request-Timeout is a transport-level header documented per-endpoint and the provenance issue matches the observed values verbatim.
